notes.scope: Floor turf around and in front of the hitting mat, putting turf, underlay and tiles. Hitting mats are a separate category.
notes.qualification: 5+ independent sources = qualified, 10+ = core. Brand pages excluded from the count. Entries with tier 'watch' are below 5 and are included for the map only; the parent decides whether they ship.
notes.verification: Every URL curl-checked 2026-10-19. Home Depot and Lowe's product pages return 403 to curl and to WebFetch (bot block); their prices come from search-result snippets of the live listing and are marked unverified.
notes.reddit: No Reddit threads surfaced in any search (site: and r/ queries returned nothing usable), so mention counts lean on golfsimulatorforum.com threads, review sites, build logs, YouTube and retailers.

products.name: Money Putt putting turf (sold as TIGS Money Putt at Shop Indoor Golf, RoS Money Putt at Rain or Shine, STI NP45 at Indoor Golf Outlet, Money Putt at Greatmats)

price.unit: per sq ft, plus $299 flat freight; 15 ft x 5 ft roll $640, 15 ft x 25 ft $1,990

other_prices.unit: per sq ft (regular $5.34), 15 ft minimum cut
STI NP45 15 ft x 5 ft; 15 ft x 10 ft $1,470

products.direct_url_note: No GrassTex maker product page found; Shop Indoor Golf is the main retailer. Greatmats spec sheet: https://www.greatmats.com/specs/grasstex/specs-grasstex-money-putt.pdf

specs.pile_height_in: 3/8 (Greatmats, Rain or Shine); Shop Indoor Golf lists 1/2
specs.face_weight: 36 oz per sq yd (Greatmats); Rain or Shine lists 63 oz per sq yd
specs.backing: ArmorLoc 3L stabilized woven PP/PET multilayer (Greatmats); polyurethane coated (Rain or Shine)
specs.stimp: 10 to 11 with no sand infill (Rain or Shine); 12 to 13 with infill (Greatmats)
specs.infill: not required; sand speeds it up
specs.colors: Forest Green, Black (Midnight Black at Rain or Shine, Bermuda Black at SIG)
specs.spec_conflicts: Resellers disagree on pile height, face weight and stimp; treat the Greatmats spec sheet as the maker number until confirmed.

products.room_fit: 15 ft roll width means a 10 ft x 15 ft bay is one seamless 15 ft x 10 ft piece (150 sq ft): about $683 plus $299 freight at Shop Indoor Golf, $980 at Rain or Shine. Cut a hitting-mat opening and inset the mat flush.
products.who_its_for: Builders who want to putt for real on the whole bay floor and want one turf for landing zone and stance area at mid price.
pros: Lies flat without glue or tape (forum, GungHo Golf)
No infill needed
Easy to cut, takes a utility knife
Sold by four sim retailers, in green and black
Stimp in the 10 to 13 range depending on infill
cons: Freight adds $299 to $300 per order at SIG; forum reports $200 to $300 per roll
Custom cuts take 3 to 5 weeks at SIG and are non-returnable
Price per 15 ft x 5 ft roll ranges from $640 to $1,040 depending on which reseller name you buy under
known_issues: Reseller spec sheets conflict (3/8 vs 1/2 in pile, 36 vs 63 oz)
Hitting full shots directly off it wears the strike zone; builders cut in a hitting strip (forum 351127)
products.why_people_choose_it: It is the putting turf the forum keeps naming at about $4 to $4.50 a foot, and GungHo Golf confirmed NP45 and Money Putt come off the same Dalton, Georgia line, so you can shop the cheapest reseller name.

products.name: Precision Putt putting turf (Classic Putt, SYNPutt at Lowe's, and dealer remnants also come up)

price.unit: 15 ft x 10 ft (about $12.07 per sq ft); 15 ft x 5 ft $1,300; 15 ft x 30 ft $4,020

other_prices.unit: per sq ft MSRP via a SYNLawn partner reseller page (search snippet, not fetched)
to $2.00 per sq ft for dealer remnants (forum, Feb 2023)

products.direct_url_note: SYNLawn golf category page (verified 200); the Precision Putt product page is linked from it but was not fetched. Lowe's SYNPutt page returns 403 to bots.

specs.face_weight: 47 oz finished pile weight; 84 oz total
specs.backing: 13PP/18PET two-part primary with 20 oz embossed rubber coating
specs.stimp: 10 to 12.5 (Indoor Golf Outlet); a forum member measured Lowe's SYNLawn at about 11

products.room_fit: One 15 ft x 10 ft piece covers a 10 ft x 15 ft bay with no seam at $1,810 from Indoor Golf Outlet; remnants from a local SYNLawn dealer are the cheap route the forum keeps recommending.
products.who_its_for: Builders who want the premium nylon putting surface and are near a SYNLawn dealer (remnants) or willing to pay the reseller price.
pros: Highest-spec nylon putting turf in the sim market; TGL's turf partner
Fast true roll, 10 to 12.5 stimp
Dealer remnants at $1.50 to $2.00 per sq ft are the forum's favorite bargain
Also sold at Lowe's cut to length (SYNPutt, Forest)
cons: Full-price reseller cuts run $9 to $17 per sq ft
Lowe's raised its minimum order (forum, 2023)
Wears in the strike zone if you hit full shots off it; builders plan to cut and replace that section
known_issues: A $600 remnant quote for 10 x 10 was called excessive on the forum; prices vary a lot by dealer
products.why_people_choose_it: It is the name every forum veteran reaches for when putting quality matters, and the remnant trick (call the local dealer) gets premium nylon for budget money.

products.name: Putting Green 6 ft wide cut to length (TMSPUTT06CTL); also Fescue Multipurpose 12 ft wide (TMCSBRN421275) and Grizzly Grass 6 ft wide (7GRBD860072H)

price.unit: per sq ft ($11.87 per linear ft at 6 ft wide), online SKU
price.verification_note: Home Depot returns 403 to curl and WebFetch; price taken from the search snippet of the live listing

other_prices.unit: per sq ft, TrafficMaster Putting Green (forum, Nov 2020)

products.direct_url_note: 403 to bots on 2026-10-19; listing exists per search index. Fescue: https://www.homedepot.com/p/TrafficMaster-Fescue-Multipurpose-12-ft-Wide-x-Cut-to-Length-Green-Artificial-Grass-Carpet-TMCSBRN421275/311276440 ; Grizzly Grass: https://www.homedepot.com/p/TrafficMaster-Grizzly-Grass-6-ft-Wide-x-Cut-to-Length-Green-Artificial-Grass-Turf-7GRBD860072H/311280619

specs.pile_height_in: not stated on the snippets read
specs.stimp: forum DIY stimp test on carpet: TrafficMaster Putting Green 10, Grizzly Grass 11 front, Garland cheap grass 9
specs.ordering: no minimum, free ship to store (forum, 2023)

products.room_fit: 6 ft rolls mean seams: two 6 ft x 15 ft strips (180 sq ft, about $356) laid across a 10 ft x 15 ft bay with one seam, or three 6 ft x 10 ft lengths. Fescue at 12 ft wide covers the width with one seam at the back.
products.who_its_for: Garage builders who want a floor that stops bounce and looks like grass for under $400 and will not putt seriously.
pros: Cheapest turf the forum rates as usable for putting (10 stimp on a DIY test)
No minimum, ship to store free
Carl's Place names the Fescue SKU in its own flooring guide
cons: 6 ft width forces seams in any bay wider than 6 ft
Thin; on bare concrete the ball still bounces hard (forum)
Not a true putting surface; the cheapest grass rolled poorly
known_issues: Store SKU (TMSPUTT0650) and online SKU (TMSPUTT06CTL) are priced differently and stock varies by store
Thicker pet-style Home Depot turf stops the ball dead, which some builders wanted and others did not
products.why_people_choose_it: It is the turf you can touch at the store, buy by the foot, and have on the floor the same afternoon; builders who later upgrade to nylon putting turf often started here.

products.name: Elite Golf Simulator Turf 15 mm (10 x 6, 12 x 6, 15 x 6 ft)

price.unit: 15 ft x 6 ft; 12 ft x 6 ft $199.99

other_prices.unit: 10 ft x 6 ft on Amazon (price tracker, Jul 2026)

products.fallback_note: Amazon ASIN not confirmed (the candidate ASIN page returned 500).

specs.install: carpet tape included; works on concrete, wood, firm carpet

products.room_fit: Each piece is only 6 ft deep, so it is a landing strip, not a floor. A 10 ft x 15 ft bay takes two 15 x 6 pieces side by side (one seam, 12 ft of depth) plus a strip at the back.
products.who_its_for: Net or screen users who want a finished-looking landing strip in front of the mat without ordering freight turf.
pros: Ships parcel, no freight
Three widths match common enclosure widths
Named top pick by four affiliate roundups
cons: 6 ft depth only
Not a putting surface; no stimp published
The only forum mention is of GoSports 4 x 5 landing mats, and that builder bought a cheaper brand at half the cost
known_issues: Roundup sites are affiliate content, not tests
Heavy roll that is not foldable
products.why_people_choose_it: It is the Amazon-easy answer for the space between mat and screen, and it matches the GoSports enclosure most of those buyers already own.

products.name: TourPutt Ultimate bulk putting turf and D-Base / O-Base / Elite-Base panel systems

price.unit: per sq ft for 150 to 300 sq ft; $5.05 at 901 to 1,500 sq ft; freight extra

other_prices.unit: to $14 per sq ft, D-Base full system plus freight; O-Base $21 to $26; Elite-Base $29 to $34
to $7,000 reseller quote for half a room (forum, Aug 2020)

specs.bases: D-Base 0.75 in molded panels (turf plus base 1 to 1.25 in); O-Base 1.0 in 2 x 2 ft panels (1.5 in total); Elite-Base 2.0 in, 23 x 23 in panels (2.5 in total, takes thick hitting mats flush)

products.room_fit: 150 sq ft is exactly the bulk minimum: $805.50 plus freight for a seamless 15 x 10 piece. A D-Base system for the same bay is roughly $1,650 to $2,100 plus freight and sets the mat flush.
products.who_its_for: Builders who want a finished putting green with a flush hitting mat and would rather buy a system than engineer a foam-and-plywood build-up.
pros: Fastest published stimp in this set (11 ft 3 in plus)
Base panels solve the flush-mat problem by design
Serving sim rooms since 2010; sells 50/50 black-green and Tour Black turf too
cons: 150 sq ft minimum on bulk turf
System pricing runs $11 to $34 per sq ft plus freight
Only one forum mention, and it was a quote the builder walked away from
known_issues: Pile height and face weight are not published on the bulk page
products.why_people_choose_it: You buy the base and the turf from one place and the mat sits flush on day one, which is the step most DIY floors get wrong.

products.name: Golf Simulator Putting Turf for Carl's Place DIY Enclosure (green, and Midnight Shadow black)
products.mention_note: Thin: two guides plus three reseller listings. Flag before shipping as qualified.

price.unit: 10 ft W x 12 ft D (Midnight Shadow at Indoor Golf Outlet); 8 x 12 $1,815; 13 x 12 $2,375

products.direct_url_note: Carl's page lists six enclosure-matched sizes (100 to 163 sq ft) but showed no price on the fetch; search index shows $1,816.95 to $2,379.95.

specs.sizes: cut and hemmed to the Carl's DIY enclosure: 8 x 8 x 5 ft enclosure takes 97.75 x 144 in (100 sq ft); 7.7 x 10 x 5 takes 122.5 x 144 in (124 sq ft); up to 161 x 144 in (163 sq ft)
specs.included: precut holes, two cups and flags; Carl's version includes foam break pads and an 18 x 36 in return strip

products.room_fit: The 10 ft wide enclosure size is 122.5 x 144 in (124 sq ft) and extends 12 in past the screen line; it fills the bay from the screen back about 12 ft, so a 15 ft deep bay has 3 ft of bare floor behind it.
products.who_its_for: Carl's DIY enclosure owners who want a matched, hemmed drop-in green with break pads rather than cutting roll goods.
pros: Pre-cut and hemmed to the enclosure, with holes and ball return
Break pads under it allow sloped putts
Fast (13 stimp) true-roll surface
cons: $15 to $18 per sq ft equivalent
Ships freight, US only
Few independent mentions; it is bought as part of the Carl's package
known_issues: Pile and backing not published on Carl's page
products.why_people_choose_it: Because it arrives already shaped to the enclosure and the break pads turn the landing zone into a practice green with slope.

products.name: SIG landing pad turf (SIG8 / SIG10 / SIG12 and SIG DIY landing pads; SIG Custom Golf Simulator Turf in Money Putt green or Bermuda Black)
products.mention_note: Thin and reseller-heavy: one review site, Indoor Golf Outlet, and package resellers. Flag before shipping as qualified.

price.unit: SIG10 landing pad 10 ft 6 in x 8 ft (compare at $999.99)

other_prices.unit: SIG DIY landing pad 8 ft 2 in wide, up to $1,299.99 at 15 ft wide
per sq ft custom cut (24 to 480 in long, 24 to 180 in wide) plus $299 freight

specs.fiber: nylon (landing pads); Bermuda Black is tufted polypropylene
specs.size: SIG10: 10 ft 6 in x 8 ft, 38 lb; DIY pad ships as two halves rolled together

products.room_fit: The SIG10 pad is 10.5 x 8 ft (84 sq ft): it fills the screen-to-mat zone of a 10 ft x 15 ft bay and leaves the stance area and the back 7 ft bare; the custom turf at $4.55 per sq ft covers the whole 150 sq ft for about $683 plus freight.
products.who_its_for: SIG enclosure owners who want the matched pad, and anyone who wants black landing turf.
pros: Sized to the enclosure, protects the floor, doubles as a putting surface
Custom cut to any size in green or black
Made in the USA
cons: $899.99 for 84 sq ft is about $10.70 per sq ft
Custom orders take 3 to 5 weeks and cannot be returned
Almost no independent discussion; forum users post the SIGPRO flooring image, not the pad
known_issues: SIG lists Money Putt pile as 1/2 in while Greatmats and Rain or Shine list 3/8 in for the same GrassTex turf
products.why_people_choose_it: It is the no-measuring option for a SIG bay, and the black version gives the floor contrast against a green hitting mat.

products.name: SIGPRO Golf Simulator Flooring (interlocking panels plus putting turf plus hitting strip)

price.unit: SIG10 size (11 ft 7 in x 15 ft 6 in); SIG8 $3,359.99; SIG12 $4,399.99

specs.included: panels, putting turf, hitting strip, four cups; flags not included; undulation foam kit is an add-on
specs.sizes: SIG10 11 ft 7 in W x 15 ft 6 in D; SIG12 13 ft 6 in W x 15 ft 6 in D

products.room_fit: The SIG10 size is 11 ft 7 in x 15 ft 6 in, so it slightly overfills a 10 ft x 15 ft bay; the SIG8 size is the fit for a 10 ft wide bay if its dimensions (image only) are under 10 ft.
products.who_its_for: Buyers who want the whole floor solved in one box: flush strip, putting green, and a base, for a SIG enclosure.
pros: Flush replaceable hitting strip with no build-up carpentry
Putting green rolls 9 to 10
Highest-rated turf product in this set with 10 reviews
cons: 2.375 in tall floor needs a transition at the room edge
Sized to SIG enclosures
known_issues: One one-star review among ten; content not read
products.why_people_choose_it: One forum member said he would rather buy the swappable flush hitting area than build his own; that is the whole pitch.

products.brand: Generic (BalanceFrom, Meister X-Thick, ProsourceFit, Harbor Freight)
products.name: Interlocking EVA foam gym tiles, 1/2 to 1.5 in, as turf underlay

price.unit: Meister X-Thick 1.5 in, 144 sq ft (forum, Mar 2023)

other_prices.unit: per 2 x 2 ft 5/8 in tile at Greatmats; 1.25 in jiu jitsu tiles about $25 per 10.89 sq ft
Rain or Shine 3/4 in high-density EVA tile, 2 x 2 ft
SimTurf 5/8 in or 1 in EVA, case of 25 (100 sq ft), range to $390

products.direct_url_note: BalanceFrom 1 in EVA puzzle mat, 6 tiles per 24 sq ft; this is the ASIN a forum builder bought to match a hitting-strip height. Amazon price not read (page too long to parse).

specs.material: EVA closed-cell foam; high-density grades sold by Rain or Shine, Ace Indoor Golf (3/4 in tatami), SimTurf
specs.height_match: 5/8 in tile plus 3/8 in putting turf = 1 in (SimTurf); 1 in tile plus 1/2 in turf meets a 1.5 in Fiberbuilt; 1.5 in Meister plus turf approaches a 2 in SIG Softy

products.room_fit: A 10 ft x 15 ft bay is 38 two-foot tiles; at 1 in that is seven 6-tile BalanceFrom packs, or 38 Rain or Shine tiles (about $1,100 at the single-tile price, less by the 30-pack).
products.who_its_for: Anyone laying turf over concrete who needs to raise the floor to the hitting mat height cheaply and wants the bay removable.
pros: Cheapest way to match turf height to the hitting mat
Kills bounce and noise on concrete (many builders)
Removable; one builder has run 1 in puzzle mats for five years and 1,000 hours
Insulates a cold slab
cons: Too spongy for some (a forum member called it squishy and swapped to firmer mats)
One builder found balls bounced twice as high over gym tiles and went back to bare concrete
Not stable under a hitting mat per GolfingSim; put the mat on rubber or plywood
Lower-density tiles compress in traffic (Carl's guide)
known_issues: Tile edges telegraph through thin turf; cover with 3/8 in plywood for a dead-flat putting surface (forum build)
products.why_people_choose_it: It is the default DIY base: cheap, cut with a knife, and it lets the hitting strip sit flush, which is the detail every build thread ends up chasing.

products.name: Golf Room Floor Tile System (1.25 in interlocking foam tiles with tapered edges and corners)

price.unit: 5-pack of 40.25 x 40.25 in tiles (about 56 sq ft); 6-pack $275.95; edge 6-packs $109.95; corner 4-pack $59.95

specs.edges: tapered depth and width edge pieces and corners for a no-trip transition
specs.use: subfloor under turf with a hitting mat or strip inset

products.room_fit: A 10 ft x 15 ft bay needs about 14 tiles (three 5-packs, about $690) plus edge packs on the open sides; Carl's recommends ordering a little extra for the interlock loss.
products.who_its_for: Builders who want a thicker, finished-edge foam base from a sim retailer rather than gym tiles.
pros: 1.25 in puts most hitting mats flush without stacking
Finished tapered edges
Sold by six sim retailers
cons: About $4 per sq ft before edges, roughly double gym tiles
Foam type and density not published
known_issues: Coverage per pack is not stated; it is a calculation
products.why_people_choose_it: It is the tile Carl's own flooring guide points to, with edge pieces that make a garage floor look finished.

products.brand: Generic (Tractor Supply stall mats, Rubber Flooring Inc rolls, Rubber-Cal)
products.name: Rubber base: 4 x 6 ft 3/4 in horse stall mats, or 3/8 to 1/2 in rubber rolls and tiles

price.unit: per sq ft, rubber tiles (GolfingSim estimate, Apr 2026); foam about $1.50

other_prices.unit: per 3 x 3 ft 5/8 in rubber interlocking tile (GSA)

products.direct_url_note: Category site; no single maker page. Tractor Supply stall mat page not fetched.

specs.mat_size: 4 x 6 ft stall mats, about 100 lb each
specs.noise_claim: GolfingSim cites Second Skin Audio: 1/2 in rubber under the hitting mat cuts perceived impact noise 35 to 50% vs bare concrete (vendor claim, not independently tested)

products.room_fit: A 10 ft x 15 ft bay is seven 4 x 6 stall mats (168 sq ft) at about 700 lb; GolfingSim prices a full 150 sq ft rubber floor at about $525 plus a 3 x 10 turf strip.
products.who_its_for: Garage builders who want a dead, durable base that also survives a car, with turf only in the hitting lane.
pros: Indestructible, keeps the ball from bouncing all over (forum)
Stable under a hitting mat where foam is not
A sulli182-style rubber roll base lets the car and the sim share the floor
cons: Heavy (a builder bought about 1,000 lb of stall mats); freight is costly so buy locally
Fresh mats from an outdoor pallet smell; let them air out
Does not look like a golf course; needs turf on top
known_issues: Stacking two stall mats to meet a 1.5 in Fiberbuilt mat works but doubles the weight
products.why_people_choose_it: It is the base that survives everything, and the hybrid rubber-floor-plus-turf-strip layout is the one most guides now recommend for garages.

products.brand: Owens Corning (FOAMULAR 150) and generic XPS / EPS
products.name: Rigid foam insulation board (1 to 1.5 in) under putting turf, usually capped with 3/8 in plywood or 1/2 in OSB

price.unit: under $300 of 1.5 in rigid foam for about 220 sq ft (forum, Oct 2022)

specs.thickness_in: 1 (Rogue Engineer, FOAMULAR 150 4 x 8 sheets, R-5) or 1.5 (forum build-ups)
specs.stack: 1.5 in foam, 3/8 in plywood glued on, 1/8 in foam underlayment, putting turf (forum JT789); or 1 in foam, double-faced tape, putting turf (Rogue Engineer)
specs.compression: rated for use under concrete slabs; does not compress under foot traffic (forum)

products.room_fit: Five 4 x 8 sheets cover a 10 ft x 15 ft bay with offcuts; cap with five sheets of 3/8 in plywood if you want a putting-flat floor.
products.who_its_for: Builders chasing a dead-flat, firm putting floor that still comes up to a 2 in hitting strip, on a budget.
pros: Firm, not spongy; one builder has had a Fiberbuilt on EPS over concrete for nine years with no issues
Cheapest way to build 1.5 in of height
Light enough to move (Rogue Engineer)
cons: Uncovered foam gets brittle and flakes; cap it
Never under the hitting area without a plywood cap, since club impact flakes it
A cheap carpet pad on top feels squishy; use thin underlayment or none
known_issues: The forum thread that proposed it never reported the final build
products.why_people_choose_it: It is how the Triple Bogey Golf and Rogue Engineer builds got a flush mat and a true putting floor for a few hundred dollars.

products.name: Petgrow / Petgrow Pro putting green turf (Amazon)

price.unit: 3 x 10 ft roll with free shipping (forum, spring 2020 purchase)

products.direct_url_note: No maker page and no confirmed Amazon ASIN found; search Amazon for Petgrow Pro Putting Green Turf 6 x 10.

specs.pile_height_in: about 1/4 (forum measurement); Pro version 0.47 in rubber-backed per roundups
specs.stimp: about 12 per the product info the reviewer found; he matched E6 to it and called it very accurate with a Mevo+

products.room_fit: Sold in small pieces, so a 10 ft x 15 ft bay means three or more seams; it is a putting strip or a hitting-zone fill, not a floor.
products.who_its_for: Budget builders who want a fast putting strip beside the mat for under $100.
pros: Cheap and fast (about 12 stimp)
A forum builder glued a cut piece to a board outdoors and it held up
Lies flat on a basement floor without anchoring
cons: Small pieces; seams everywhere on a full floor
Creasing from shipping is the common complaint (roundup)
known_issues: A forum builder laid Petgrow Pro over 1/8 in underlayment on plywood over foam; reported soft-firm after one month, no long-term report
products.why_people_choose_it: It is the sub-$100 Amazon putting turf with a forum review that says the stimp number was real.

products.name: NP50 / NP55 texturized nylon putting turf (and PL306 One Putt with 5 mm foam backing)

price.unit: NP50 15 ft x 5 ft, from (Indoor Golf Outlet)

other_prices.unit: per sq ft plus shipping for NP50 in 2014; PL306 about $4 per sq ft in 2016 (forum)

products.direct_url_note: STI's own product page was not found; Indoor Golf Outlet is the sim retailer carrying NP45, NP50, NP55 and Fast Putt.

specs.backing: heavy rubber (NP50); PL306 carries a 5 mm foam back for concrete
specs.rank: Indoor Golf Outlet ranks NP45 just below NP50 and NP55
specs.mill: Grass Turf Mills, Dalton, Georgia; sister company to GrassTex (forum)

products.room_fit: 15 ft roll: one 15 x 10 piece for a 10 ft x 15 ft bay; buy from an authorized STI rep, since the forum found online resellers charging much more.
products.who_its_for: Builders near an STI dealer who want top-tier nylon and have been told to buy direct.
pros: Top-tier nylon; same mill family as Money Putt
PL306's foam back is the forum's preferred answer for turf straight on concrete
Available in black at Indoor Golf Outlet
cons: Reseller prices are high; a 15 x 5 is $1,125 vs $640 for Money Putt
Dealer network, not a web cart
known_issues: The same product is sold under several names, which confuses price comparison
products.why_people_choose_it: The forum's long-time turf voice (cspin) buys STI through a rep and tells everyone else to do the same.

products.name: RoS Landing Pad Turf (compact 5 x 8 to 5 x 12; 10 x 10 bundle) and Studio Turf full-floor kit

price.unit: 5 x 8 ft compact; 5 x 10.5 $399; 5 x 12 $449; 10 x 10 bundle $780 (compare at $899); Studio Turf 11 ft 6 in x 14 ft 6 in $4,000, 13 ft 2 in x 16 ft 2 in $4,500

specs.usable_area: about 7 x 7 ft on the 10 x 10 bundle
specs.fiber: putting green turf; Studio Turf is nylon
specs.pairs_with: SwingTurf mat; also Fiberbuilt, TrueStrike, CCE

products.room_fit: The 10 x 10 bundle covers the front two-thirds of a 10 ft x 15 ft bay; the Studio Turf 11 ft 6 in x 14 ft 6 in kit is a near-exact full-floor match at $4,000.

Sizes match the SwingBay packages
Multi-year warranty

1 in pile is a landing surface, not a putting speed

products.name: TFD Putting Elite (and Nylon 36 padded, Birdie Putt Elite, Putt Putt)

price.unit: per sq ft, Putting Elite; Birdie Putt Elite $2.89; Putt Putt $1.99

specs.infill: TFD suggests its 30/50 putting green infill as an add-on

products.room_fit: 15 ft roll; 150 sq ft of Putting Elite is about $599 plus shipping.
products.who_its_for: Budget builders who want nylon putting turf under $4 a foot and padded nylon for the lane.

Padded nylon option named by a 2026 build thread and by the OnTheGreen budget guide
GungHo Golf pointed a wet-garage builder here
cons: Four mentions, not five
No stimp published
products.why_people_choose_it: Cheapest nylon putting turf with a rubber back that the forum has actually pointed people to.

products.name: PreGra 62 oz Select artificial turf, 15 ft wide by the linear foot (also 50 oz Premium and All-Purpose rolls)
products.mention_note: Zero sim-builder mentions; all four are general turf-buying sources. Included because the brief asked about Costco.

price.unit: price not shown on the fetched page; the YouTube title quotes $124 for a 3.75 x 12.5 ft PreGra roll (different SKU)

specs.infill: PreGra listings say all PreGra turf requires infill for proper installation (search snippet)
specs.reviews: 0 member reviews on the fetched page

products.room_fit: 15 ft wide, so one 10 ft length covers a 10 ft x 15 ft bay; but 1.75 in landscape pile is rough-length, holds a ball dead and is not a putting surface.
products.who_its_for: Nobody in the sim sources; a landscape turf that garage builders ask about because the price is low.

Warehouse pickup, no freight
cons: Requires infill per the maker
1.75 in pile is far taller than any sim turf (3/8 to 1 in)
No sim build found using it
products.why_people_choose_it: They do not, in any source found; it is the question that gets asked, and the answer is that the pile is too long.

products.name: Golf Simulator Turf 2-in-1 (tour-grade putting green with optional 3 x 5 hitting turf)

price.unit: base (7.5 ft wide x 8 ft); length to 18 ft; optional 3 x 5 hitting turf plus $185; hole-deepening shims plus $99

specs.features: no seam, drop-in cups, heavy rubber bumpers, portable, indoor or outdoor

products.room_fit: 7.5 ft wide x 15 ft long fits a 10 ft x 15 ft bay as a center runner with 15 in of bare floor each side; the garage build in Sim Weekly raised it on foam squares to meet the mat.
products.who_its_for: Garage builders who want a portable, seamless green they can lift out when the car comes in.
pros: Seamless, portable, bumpers keep balls on it
Published stimp
The one garage build log that named its upgrade path went Home Depot turf to BirdieBall
cons: Repeated full swings wear the center; the hitting turf is an add-on
Not full-width

blog_outline.title: Turf for a garage golf simulator: it is a floor, not a mat
sections: Turf is a floor, not a mat: the mat takes the club, the turf takes the ball and your feet; what pile height means (3/8 in putting, 1/2 in landing, 1 in looks, 1.75 in landscape is too tall)
The three jobs the floor does: stop the bounce (the screen causes most of it), let the mat sit flush, give you something to putt on

How much to buy for a 10 x 15 bay: rolls are 15 ft wide, so buy 10 running feet and lay it sideways for zero seams; 6 ft Home Depot rolls mean a seam; add 5 to 10 percent and plan the hitting-mat cutout

What goes under it on concrete: bare slab (cheap, loud, bouncy), EVA tiles (1/2 to 1.5 in, cheap, sometimes spongy), rubber stall mats or rolls (dead and car-proof), rigid foam capped with plywood (flat and firm), or a 2x4 and plywood platform; vapor barrier in basements
Getting the mat flush: stack math worked for Fiberbuilt (1.5 in), SIG Softy (2 to 2.375 in) and Country Club Elite (3/4 in); why the one thing you cannot fix later is a floor that is too tall
Putting turf speed: what stimp 9 to 13 feels like, why new turf speeds up, sand infill, and matching the sim software green speed to your floor
The two-name problem: Money Putt, NP45, TIGS and RoS are one GrassTex turf; shop the cheapest label and read the spec sheet

Budget ladder with 2026 prices: Home Depot TrafficMaster at $1.98, TFD Putting Elite at $3.99, Money Putt at $4.55 plus freight, Pro Putt bulk at $5.37, SYNLawn at $9 to $17 per foot (or remnants at $2), and the all-in-one SIGPRO floor at $3,360 to $4,400
Black turf: it is sold for looks and contrast, not for launch monitors; no source ties floor-turf color to ball detection
Cutting, seaming, holding it down: acclimate it, trim with a utility knife, carpet tape or seam tape at joints, heavy turf lies flat on its own, Velcro squares for a removable strip, no metal spikes
Static and infill indoors: static is a first-six-months thing on new turf, treat with a wetting agent; most sim putting turf needs no infill, sand brushed in makes it faster

The fold-away bay where the car parks on the floor: what driveway turf makers say (occasional parking fine, turning wheels tears fibers, daily parking compacts), what forum garages actually do (rubber or carpet-tile base in the tire path, turf rolled up or tarped, a hoist to the ceiling), and the layout that works: hard floor where the tires go, turf only in the lane. Mention that a fold-flat enclosure like StowGolf keeps the bay clear for the car, with the disclosure sentence: Disclosure: Brett Martin runs Teed and builds StowGolf.
Reference bag: the qualified products by subtype with direct links and one forum thread each
